chapter: Connie's Inn, Duke Ellington and the Swingland band
title: A night's schedule at Swingland: dance sets and two shows
summary: The band played 45 minutes of dance music, then a show of up to ninety minutes, dance sets, and a second different show to hold the crowd.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: : Yeah. That's great. I'd like to ask some questions before we really continue on the years here. Something about -- some musical questions. When you were playing these ballrooms such as this -- of course, you were doing reviews, did you play only the show or did you play for dance music in between, or concertized, or -- how did that work out?
Well, at Swingland, we're talking about that now -- well, the band would come to work, you know,

like at 9:00, and we would play for 45 minutes, you know, dance music, and then we'd take our fifteen minute break, and the first show of the evening would go on. Then we would play the show, which would last anywhere from an hour and fifteen minutes to an hour and a half. It all depends if the audience was quite responsive, naturally you stretch it out, you know. Then just before the break, we would always play a couple of numbers for dance set, dancing, and then make our usual announcement that the band was going to take an intermission, and we'd be back with you very shortly. "And ^ Don't forget, we have another show entirely different from the one that you've just seen," you know. And that show would come on until the last hour of the morning, that is, to hold the people, see.
